stops.note: a trade weight of about 600 grams used across Southeast Asian ports; European merchants also used it for the matching Chinese unit, the jīn
the East India Company weighed Canton tea in catties and piculs (100 catties); Hong Kong law today still defines the catty as 604.79 grams
a small box holding about a catty of tea; tea was so costly in the 1700s that caddies came with locks (golf's 'caddie' is unrelated, from French cadet)

current_meaning: a small container for storing tea
